alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
alternates.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
alternates.line: This calm you describe, Krishna, I can't see it lasting. My mind is too restless.
alternates.translation: Arjuna said: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana, I do not see how it can last, because of restlessness.
alternates.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

alternates.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.

prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: After the story of two grieving brothers, Vasishtha tells Rama how worry feeds itself.
verse.sanskrit: चिन्तनेनैधते चिन्ता त्विन्धनेनेव पावकः । नश्यत्यचिन्ततेनैव विनेन्धनमिवानलः ॥
verse.line: Worry grows when you feed it thought, like fire with fuel. Starve it, and it dies down.
verse.translation: Worry grows by thinking, as fire grows with fuel; and it dies by not being thought, as fire dies without fuel.
verse.why: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

prasang.title: Punya consoles his younger brother Pavana after their parents die
prasang.summary: Two brothers live with their parents by the Ganga. When their father and mother die, the elder, Punya, performs the rites calmly while the younger, Pavana, wanders the forest weeping. Punya gently helps him see that the bonds of 'mine' and 'not mine' are made in the mind. Vasishtha draws the lesson: worry grows when fed, and a full mind finds the world full.
prasang.story_hook: When their parents died, one brother quietly lit the funeral fires and the other ran weeping into the forest.
prasang.lesson: Grief is love; endless rumination is the part we can learn to stop feeding.

verse.for_you: Your mind is giving the same old scene fuel at 2am. You do not have to watch it burn.
verse.try_today: Notice one thought you are feeding today and stop feeding it.

why: Worry grows when you feed it (Yoga Vasishtha 5.21.6)
worry is shown to live on the attention it is fed

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verse.line: Practice is good, understanding better, meditation better still. But letting go of results brings peace at once.
verse.translation: Knowledge is better than mere practice; meditation is better than knowledge; giving up the fruit of action is better than meditation. From that renunciation, peace follows immediately.
verse.why: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.
verse.misuse: Not 'stop caring how things turn out'. Peace comes from releasing the grip, not from indifference.

prasang.title: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

verse.for_you: You are caught in the loop of a past conversation, replaying every word. The mind is trying to fix what is already finished. Peace is not in finding the right thing to say. Peace is in letting the fruit of that moment go.
verse.try_today: Notice when the loop begins and name one detail you cannot change.

why: Peace follows at once from letting go of the fruit.
peace is placed right after releasing the grip on results, not after mastering meditation

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha describes King Janaka after his awakening, still ruling his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: भविष्यं नानुसंधत्ते नातीतं चिन्तयत्यसौ । वर्तमाननिमेषं तु हसन्नेवानुवर्तते ॥
verse.line: Don't chase the future or brood on the past. Meet this moment with a smile.
verse.translation: He does not chase the future or brood on the past; he simply goes along with the present moment, smiling.
verse.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

prasang.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
prasang.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
prasang.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

verse.scene_line: You sit on the edge of the bed, and the past keeps knocking, but the present moment waits with a smile.

why: Do not chase the future or brood on the past.
a picture of a mind not living ahead or behind

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: Raja-Yoga (1896), chapter 6: the first practice for a racing mind.
verse.line: Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch.
verse.translation: The first lesson, then, is to sit for some time and let the mind run on. The mind is bubbling up all the time. It is like that monkey jumping about. Let the monkey jump as much as he can; you simply wait and watch. … But you will find that each day the mind's vagaries are becoming less and less violent, that each day it is becoming calmer.
verse.why: Watch the mind before trying to control it; calm comes with daily practice.

prasang.title: The drunken monkey: taming a restless mind
prasang.summary: The mind is a monkey made drunk by desire, stung by jealousy and possessed by pride. The first practice is to sit and watch it without fighting; each day it grows calmer. Then take up one idea and let it fill your life.
prasang.story_hook: There was a monkey, restless as all monkeys are; someone gave it wine, then a scorpion stung it, and then a demon got into it.
prasang.lesson: Watch the mind before trying to control it; calm comes with daily practice.

verse.for_you: You keep replaying that 2019 conversation at 2am. The mind is a monkey, and it is allowed to jump. You do not have to wrestle it into silence tonight.
verse.try_today: Sit and let the mind jump while you wait and watch.
verse.scene_line: You watch the monkey of your mind jump about the room from 2019.

why: calm arrives by itself, day by day
a sitting practice to repeat

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: न वैरमुद्दिपयति प्रशान्तं / न दर्पमारोहति शान्तिमेति / न दुर्गतोऽस्मीति करोत्यकार्यं / तमार्यशीलं परमाहुरार्याः
verse.line: Don't rake up settled quarrels, don't ride your pride, and don't excuse wrongdoing because times are hard.
verse.translation: He does not rekindle a quarrel that has died down, does not climb onto his pride, stays calm, and does not do wrong telling himself 'I am in a bad way': the noble call such conduct the best.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

why: A calmed enmity is left calm
Hard times are not taken as licence

story.title: Young Uddalaka sits down to meditate and his mind will not stay
story.story_hook: A young sage sat down to meditate and his mind ran off within moments. He kept failing for a long time. Then he tried something different.
story.summary: Uddalaka is young, proud and serious. He longs for a calm mind: 'When will I rest in that stillness? When will my mind stop swinging between liking and disliking?' He sits in meditation in the forest, and his monkey-like mind runs to the objects of the senses.
story.lesson: A restless mind is not overcome by force but by patient return and clear inquiry into what one is.
story.teaser: A young sage sat down to meditate and his mind ran off within moments. He kept failing for a long time. Then he tried something different.
story.for_you: That conversation from 2019 keeps replaying at two in the morning because you are still asking what it means. The mind will not stay still by force. You can return to it with patience and ask what you are in that moment.

verse.speaker: Nidagha
verse.sanskrit: इतश्चेतश्च सुव्यग्रं व्यर्थमेवाभिधावति । मनो दूरतरं याति ग्रामे कौलेयको यथा ॥
verse.line: The mind runs here and there for nothing, wandering far like a stray village dog.
verse.translation: The mind runs here and there, restless and pointless; it wanders far away, like a dog in a village.
verse.why: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

verse.for_you: Your mind runs here and there for nothing, like a stray village dog. The conversation from 2019 is just a sound it keeps chasing. Let it wander without following.
verse.try_today: Notice when your mind runs here and there, and let it be a stray village dog.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the dark, while the mind runs here and there for nothing, like a stray dog in a village.

why: a seeker describes his own mind running everywhere for nothing
My mind runs everywhere for nothing, and every good quality I take up, craving chews through. What do I do?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: आशा नाम नदी मनोरथजला तृष्णातरङ्गाकुला रागग्राहवती वितर्कविहगा धैर्यद्रुमध्वंसिनी । मोहावर्तसुदुस्तरातिगहना प्रोत्तुङ्गचिन्तातटी तस्याः पारगता विशुद्धमनसो नन्दन्ति योगीश्वराः ॥
verse.line: Hope is a river: its water is wishes, its waves are craving, and its high banks are worry.
verse.translation: There is a river called Hope. Its water is wishes, its waves are craving; passions are its crocodiles, doubts its birds; it uproots the trees of courage; its whirlpools of delusion are hard to cross and deep, and its banks of worry tower high. Only great yogis, pure in mind, who reach the far shore, rejoice.
verse.why: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
prasang.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
prasang.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

verse.for_you: Your mind replays that old conversation, caught in the current of hope. The water is wish, the waves are craving, and the banks are worry. You are not on the far shore today.
verse.try_today: Notice when a wish turns into a craving. Watch the worry bank rise.
verse.scene_line: You sit alone in the dark, watching the river of hope carry you back to 2019.

why: The river called Hope (Bhartrihari, Vairagya Shataka 10)
Craving as the waves

verse.speaker: The Ajagara sage
verse.setting: A wandering sage who lives like the python, taking what comes, explains his contentment to Prahlada.
verse.sanskrit: न सन्निपतितं धर्म्यमुपभोगं यदृच्छया / प्रत्याचक्षे न चाप्येनमनुरुध्ये सुदुर्लभम्
verse.line: I don't refuse good things that come to me, and I don't chase what's hard to get.
verse.translation: I do not refuse a rightful pleasure that comes to me on its own, nor do I go chasing after one that is hard to get.
verse.why: Take what comes gladly; stop chasing what's out of reach.

prasang.title: The python-sage (Ajagara vrata)
prasang.summary: Prahlada meets a sage who lives like a python, taking what comes and not chasing. The sage explains how ceasing to chase made him content.
prasang.lesson: Take what comes gladly; stop chasing what's out of reach.

verse.for_you: Your mind replays 2019, but the past is already held. Let the conversation rest. The mind that stops chasing what is lost finds what is present.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing that arrived without your asking today.
verse.scene_line: Like the sage who takes what the path offers, you let the conversation go.

why: What others do is theirs; pair rule applies.
No chasing

verse.speaker: Pingala (quoted by Bhishma)
verse.setting: Pingala, left waiting all night by a lover who never came, finally lets go and finds peace.
verse.sanskrit: सुखं निराशः स्वपिति नैराश्यं परमं सुखम् / आशामनाशां कृत्वा हि सुखं स्वपिति पिङ्गला
verse.line: Pingala let go of her expectation and slept peacefully. Letting go of expectation is the greatest ease.
verse.translation: The one free of expectation sleeps in peace; freedom from expectation is the highest happiness. Turning hope into no-hope, Pingala sleeps peacefully.
verse.why: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.
verse.misuse: This is about clinging to an outcome, not about giving up hope in life.

prasang.title: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting
prasang.summary: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
prasang.story_hook: Pingala sat awake listening for footsteps that never came, until she stopped listening.
prasang.lesson: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.

verse.for_you: Your peace does not depend on a reply from the past. The replaying is the waiting. Let the expectation go and sleep.
verse.try_today: Notice when the mind is waiting for a different outcome and let it rest.
verse.scene_line: You lie awake at two in the morning, replaying a conversation from 2019, letting go of the expectation that it can be fixed.

why: Dropping the expectation is the ease.
The waiting itself is shown as the pain, and its end as rest

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
verse.line: Little by little, with patience and steady resolve, settle the mind and let other thoughts go.
verse.translation: Little by little one should come to rest, with understanding held steady; fixing the mind on the self, one should think of nothing else.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.for_you: That voice at 2am is still arguing with a version of you from 2019. You can let the replay fade without fixing what it said. Steady resolve is enough to quiet it tonight.
verse.try_today: Notice one thought, and gently return the mind to the room.

why: the mind resting in the self
Little by little, with patience.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: परिभ्रमसि किं मुधा क्वचन चित्त विश्राम्यतां स्वयं भवति यद्यथा भवति तत्तथा नान्यथा । अतीतमननुस्मरन्नपि च भाव्यसंकल्पयन् नतर्कितसमागमाननुभवामि भोगानहम् ॥
verse.line: Why wander, mind? Rest. Not replaying the past, not scripting the future, I take what comes.
verse.translation: Why do you wander about in vain, mind? Rest somewhere. Whatever is to happen happens just as it will, and not otherwise. Not recalling the past, not planning the future, I enjoy the pleasures that come to me unlooked-for.
verse.why: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.
verse.misuse: Not an argument against planning; it is for the worry loop once you have done your part.

prasang.title: Vairagyashatakam: Advice to the mind
prasang.summary: The poet talks to his own mind: why exhaust yourself pleasing others, why replay the past and script the future, why roam everywhere but within. 'So what?' asks what all our gains amount to.
prasang.lesson: Stop seeking approval and rehearsing outcomes; the calm you want is already inside.

verse.for_you: Your mind is a room where a conversation from 2019 is playing on loop, and you are standing in its doorway, unable to leave. The verse says to stop wandering and rest somewhere. Let the night pass without replaying what was said, and let the morning come without scripting what should be said.
verse.try_today: When the loop starts, notice the room you are in and name one thing in front of you.

why: Vishramyatam

story.title: Kabir to his own restless mind: slowly, slowly
story.story_hook: The gardener can pour a hundred pots of water. The mango still waits for its season.
story.summary: The mind wants the result now. Kabir talks to it the way a gardener would.
story.lesson: Water faithfully; the fruit comes in its season, not because you poured more.
story.teaser: The gardener can pour a hundred pots of water. The mango still waits for its season.
story.for_you: You are replaying a conversation from years ago, trying to force a result that is no longer in your hands. You keep pouring water into the past, but the fruit of that moment will not ripen on your schedule. Let the water be enough today, and let the season be its own.

plan_v3.path: st.bhakti.kabir_slowly_mind -enacts_in-> chanchalya, chinta, trishna ; st.bhakti.kabir_slowly_mind -enacts_turn-> dhriti, shanti
why: Water faithfully; the fruit comes in its season, not because you poured more.

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call a mind that won't settle, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.insight: Your mind was never taught to rest, so it keeps running long after you've asked it to stop.

I can't sleep, my mind is racing
I'm anxious about how things will turn out
I feel anxious most of the time
I feel like an imposter

queries.hook: I can't stop overthinking. Inside, my mind won't settle, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.
queries.steady: The mind can be trained slowly, by practice and letting go; each time it wanders, it can be gently brought back.
queries.act: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.
queries.story: A story of a seeker whose mind will not settle, facing a mind that won't settle.

understanding.life_context: Working. Feels restless; closest to "I can't stop overthinking" and "I can't focus, my mind is restless".

plan_v3.first_line: Your mind keeps replaying a conversation from 2019, and this restless monkey reaches even where it cannot go.

verse.speaker: Nidagha
verse.sanskrit: यां यामहं मुनिश्रेष्ठ संश्रयामि गुणश्रियम् । तां तां कृन्तति मे तृष्णा तन्त्रीमिव कुमूषिका ॥
verse.line: Every good quality I take up, craving gnaws through, like a mouse chewing a string.
verse.translation: Whatever good quality I take refuge in, great sage, craving cuts it away, as a mouse gnaws through a string.
verse.why: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

prasang.title: Nidagha's lament
prasang.summary: Young Nidagha returns from pilgrimage disillusioned and pours out his heart to his teacher Ribhu: life is fleeting, the mind runs like a stray dog, craving gnaws every good quality, and mastering the mind is harder than drinking the ocean.
prasang.lesson: Naming how restless your mind is, is where peace begins.

verse.for_you: You sit in the dark with a conversation from years ago. The mind chews on what was said and what was not. No quality holds when the craving gnaws.
verse.try_today: Notice the mind chewing on one thought and let the string go slack.

why: My mind runs everywhere for nothing, and every good quality I take up, craving chews through. What do I do?
first person: every resolve I make, craving chews through

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna explains the three qualities: clarity, restlessness and dullness.
verse.sanskrit: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥
verse.line: When restlessness rules: greed, constant activity, starting project after project, craving and no peace.
verse.translation: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and craving: these arise when rajas increases, best of the Bharatas.
verse.why: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

prasang.title: Sattva, rajas, tamas: the three gunas
prasang.summary: Sattva binds through attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas through craving and activity, tamas through laziness and sleep. Each shows itself in recognisable signs.
prasang.lesson: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

verse.try_today: When the mind replays that conversation, notice the craving for a different ending.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the quiet of the night while Krishna speaks of the signs of a restless mind.

why: What each guna yields (Bhagavad Gita 14.17)
the unrest is named as a rise of rajas, a passing quality of nature, and not as the person

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: यदि देहं पृथक् कृत्य चिति विश्राम्य तिष्ठसि । अधुनैव सुखी शान्तो बन्धमुक्तो भविष्यसि ॥
verse.line: Step back from the body, rest as awareness, and right now you can be happy, calm and free.
verse.translation: If you set the body apart and rest in awareness, then this very moment you will be happy, at peace and free of bondage.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.for_you: That replay from 2019 is still running in the body. Step back from the body, and rest as the awareness watching it. You can be calm and free right now.
verse.try_today: Notice the thought, then rest as the awareness behind it.
verse.scene_line: You watch the old conversation repeat while Janaka rests as awareness, free of it all.

why: resting in awareness is offered as a place the restless mind can stop
the promise is peace now, not after the problem is solved

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks how one beyond the three qualities lives; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: उदासीनवदासीनो गुणैर्यो न विचाल्यते । गुणा वर्तन्त इत्येव योऽवतिष्ठति नेङ्गते ॥
verse.line: Sit like a witness, unshaken, knowing it's just moods moving through, and stay steady.
verse.translation: who sits like one unconcerned, unshaken by the qualities, who knows 'it is only the qualities moving' and stays firm without wavering,
verse.why: Let moods come and go without fighting or chasing them.

prasang.title: Going beyond the gunas
prasang.summary: One beyond the qualities does not hate moods when they come or long for them when they go, sits like a witness, and is the same in praise and blame, honour and insult.
prasang.lesson: Let moods come and go without fighting or chasing them.

verse.try_today: Notice one mood passing through you today as a witness.
verse.scene_line: Arjuna sits as a witness to the gunas, and so do you.

why: Let the monkey jump; wait and watch.
the churn is the gunas moving; one can sit as its witness

verse.speaker: Bodhya
verse.setting: Bodhya describes another of his teachers to King Yayati: an arrow-maker lost in his work.
verse.sanskrit: इषुकारो नरः कश्चिदिषावासक्तमानसः / समीपेनापि गच्छन्तं राजानं नावबुद्धवान्
verse.line: An arrow-maker was so absorbed in his work, he didn't notice the king walking past.
verse.translation: A certain arrow-maker was so absorbed in his arrow that he did not even notice the king passing right beside him.
verse.why: Learn from everything. Drop what makes you a target, and give your work full attention.

prasang.title: Bodhya's teachers
prasang.summary: Asked how he found peace, the sage Bodhya names his teachers: Pingala, the osprey that dropped its scrap of meat and was left alone, the snake, the deer, the arrow-maker so absorbed he did not see the king pass, and a girl's bangle.
prasang.lesson: Learn from everything. Drop what makes you a target, and give your work full attention.

verse.for_you: The mind keeps replaying that 2019 conversation because it is still trying to finish the sentence. It is not a mistake you made; it is a thought that is still working.
verse.try_today: Notice one small detail of your immediate task and give it your full attention for a moment.
verse.scene_line: The arrow-maker did not notice the king, and you are missing the room around your thoughts.

why: Absorption as rest from distraction
Single-pointed attention to the work in hand

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha's closing advice to Rama on living in the world after the three vows.
verse.sanskrit: अन्तर्मुखः सन्सततं समस्तं कुर्वन्बहिष्ठं खलु कार्यजातम् । न खेदमायासि कदाचिदेव निराकृताहंकृतितामुपैषि ॥
verse.line: Stay anchored within while you do all your outer work, and you won't burn out.
verse.translation: Staying turned inward while doing all the outer work that comes to you, you will never grow weary, and you will be free of the sense of being the doer.
verse.why: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

prasang.title: Shiva's three vows: be a great doer, enjoyer and letter-go
prasang.summary: Vasishtha gives Rama three vows that Shiva once gave his devotee Bhringi: be a great doer, a great enjoyer, and a great renouncer. A great doer acts fully and on time without clinging; a great enjoyer takes in joys and sorrows evenly, like the ocean takes in rivers; a great renouncer lets go inside. Live this way and work won't wear you out.
prasang.lesson: Work fully, enjoy fully, let go fully; anchored inside, you can do it all without burning out.

verse.for_you: That 2019 conversation still has its hooks in you. The outer work of your life keeps piling up. You can stay turned inward while it does, and the sense of being the doer will fall away.
verse.try_today: Notice where your attention is right now. Let it rest there without fixing the past.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the dark, and Vasishtha tells Rama that the ocean takes in rivers without becoming the river.

why: an inner anchor during activity

story.title: Bhima cannot bear to wait thirteen years
story.story_hook: He found a loophole: count thirteen months as thirteen years. His brother said no.
story.summary: Bhima is sick of waiting. The years we wait, he tells Yudhishthira, are years off our lives, and death does not pause for a pledge. He even offers a scholar's loophole: the texts allow a substitute, so count the thirteen months we have already lived here as thirteen years, and let us go and fight now.
story.lesson: A pledge is not broken by a clever reading of it; time that must be waited out can be spent getting ready.
story.teaser: He found a loophole: count thirteen months as thirteen years. His brother said no.
story.for_you: The past conversation replays because it is unfinished. The waiting for a better answer can become the work of finding it. You are preparing for the next time you speak.

why: A pledge is not broken by a clever reading of it; time that must be waited out can be spent getting ready.
